representation: IEEE-754 binary32 bit pattern stored in MSL uint; arithmetic uses integer operations only
implemented: classification: sign, zero, finite, infinity, quiet NaN, signaling NaN
sign, absolute-value, and sign-bit negation operations
binary32 multiply using an exact 48-bit integer product
binary32 divide using restoring quotient generation and sticky remainder
ordered equality and relational comparisons; unordered NaN results
binary32-bit to binary64-bit exact widening conversion
binary64-bit to binary32-bit RN-even conversion with gradual underflow
correctly rounded binary32 square root using integer radicand and gradual-underflow packing

special_values.zero: signed zeros are preserved by sign operations, multiplication, division, and widening; exact cancellation returns positive zero under RN-even
special_values.underflow: gradual; subnormal results are rounded rather than flushed
special_values.overflow: finite arithmetic and narrowing conversion round to signed infinity when the rounded exponent exceeds the binary32 range
special_values.nan_arithmetic: the first NaN operand is quieted while preserving its sign and payload; invalid non-NaN operations return canonical positive quiet NaN
special_values.nan_conversion: NaNs are quieted; narrowing keeps high payload bits and widening places the binary32 payload in the high binary64 fraction bits
special_values.nan_comparison: all ordered comparisons return false; soft32_compare returns 2 for unordered

unimplemented: remainder, modulo, nextafter, scalbn, and frexp
transcendental functions including log, exp, and pow
directed rounding modes and IEEE exception flags
NaN totalOrder and signaling exception behavior
verification: MetalToolchain 27.1 compiled and executed temporary probes on the installed Apple GPU. A deterministic 256-lane boundary/pseudo-random finite probe emitted 5,888 words; bounded comparisons returned zero mismatches. A separate 59-lane edge probe made 1,121 oracle comparisons with zero mismatches, including signed zero, qNaN/sNaN payload quieting, invalid-operation NaNs, int32/uint32 conversion boundaries, and binary64-to-binary32 rounding ties. This remains bounded evidence; it does not exhaust all IEEE input space or consumer-specific CUDA behavior, so the contract status remains implemented-unverified.
